t:
(a) Program Extension.—Section 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4026) is amended by striking “the earlier of the date of the enactment into law of an Act that specifically amends the date specified in this section or May 31, 2012” and inserting “July 31, 2012”. 
    (b) Financing.—Section 1309(a) of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a)) is amended by striking “the earlier of the date of the enactment into law of an Act that specifically amends the date specified in this section or May 31, 2012” and inserting “July 31, 2012”.

fable.w: The section only extends the National Flood Insurance Program's authorization and financing dates to July 31, 2012 by amending two statutory date references. The tempting reading is that extending a program touching the public implies outside involvement, but the text contains no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends statutory dates for program extension and financing. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for outside input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Section 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4026) is amended by striking “the earlier of the date of the enactment into law of an Act that specifically amends the date specified in this section or May 31, 2012” and inserting “July 31, 2012”.

opus.w: This section only extends the flood insurance program and its financing authority to July 31, 2012, by replacing a date in two statutory sections. It does not mention consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or any right to sue. Being about a federal program is not enough to count as participation.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to treat a change to the National Flood Insurance Program as a federal decision that outsiders might weigh in on. That fails: the section only swaps one date for another and has no process involving anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section merely amends statutory dates for program extension and financing. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. There are no mentions of advisory boards, hearings, or coordination with states or the public.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending dates for a program extension implies a decision-making process involving stakeholders. However, the text itself only specifies the new dates and does not mention any consultation, public comment, or advisory bodies.
